newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rise in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rise in quiet trade.

text.p: Egyptian shares rose for the second consecutive day on Thursday in trade dominated by Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index rose 1.14 points to 389.01 in average volume of 53.52 million pounds ($15.76 million).

"Volumes were normal today, there wasn't anything too exciting," said broker Elwi Taymour of EFG/Hermes. "For the past couple of years April has been a quiet month because it has a lot of holidays. Things should start to get exciting in May."
Abu Qir led the day's 10 most active shares, rising 0.50 pounds to 102.00 after trade worth almost six million pounds.
"Foreign insitutions are not allowed to trade in Abu Qir so it looks like it's local mutual funds and insurance companies that have created this trade," Taymour said.
The firm said earlier this month it would issue 8,232,760 new shares to increase its capital by about 21.8 percent from 151 million pounds.
Shareholders can buy a minumum of five shares and a maximum of 21.8 percent of their holdings at 45.00 pounds per share when the closed issue opens for one month from April 29.

The popular housing firm Medinet Nasr Housing and Development was the day's second most actively traded stock, closing 3.25 pounds higher at 493.25 after shares worth almost five million pounds changed hands.
"The stock market has given the green light for the company to go ahead with the share split," Taymour said.
The company had to postpone last month its one-for-one free share offer because of a technical hitch and had to wait for the stock exchange to agree to register the capital increase.
Cement shares were some of the day's strongest performers, with Amriya Cement leading the way. The stock closed 0.39 higher at 89.40 after trade worth 4.01 million pounds.
Helwan Portland Cement closed unchanged at 79.00 while Egyptian Tora Portland Cement rose 0.75 pounds to 97.00
"There's volume in the cement sector. Prices haven't jumped but they are quite stable. It's a healthy sign for the market," Taymour told Reuters.
Commercial International Bank ended higher for the second consecutive day, rising 2.89 pounds to 85.00 after trade in more than three million pounds
The index for openly traded firms rose to 590.58 from 588.04 points on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 272.09 from 271.51.
Of the 83 shares traded, 27 rose, 28 declined and 28 remained unchanged.
